subject: Dedicated capacity: hardware preferences, TPS & concurrency follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mitchell <aaron.mitchell@zenity.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@zenity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: hardware preferences, TPS & concurrency follow-up

Hi Aaron / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can model a dedicated-capacity recommendation: 

TL;DR: you indicated a strong preference toward predictable latency for inference at peak load, 99th percentile latency target ~120–150ms per token, and an initial target of ~250 TPS for short-chat flows (average request ~350 tokens). You also mentioned batch/async background jobs for embeddings at lower priority.

Open items we promised to capture:
- Confirm GPU family preference (H100 vs A100 vs mixed pool) and willingness to consider quantized variants (8-bit) for cost savings.
- Clarify peak concurrency (concurrent live chats) vs sustained TPS. You mentioned spikes of ~600 concurrent users during promotions; please confirm concurrent sessions vs average RTT.
- Token mix: estimate of short chat (<=512 tokens) vs long assist (1k+ tokens). I sketched numbers in the attached workbook — please update.
- VPC requirement: you flagged wanting a private VPC for PHI-sensitive flows. If Private deployment is required, we need to confirm network controls and expected bandwidth between your VPC and Redwood Dedicated.

Attachments: zenity-sizing-workbook.xlsx (I prefilled with today’s call numbers), redwood-deploy-options.pdf (short explainer on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Next steps we recommend:
1) Aaron/Priya: update the sizing workbook with token-mix columns by Monday so Ben/Karthik can run a hardware fit.
2) Ben / Karthik: produce 2 SKU options (performance-optimized H100 pool, and cost-optimized A100/mixed pool with 8-bit quantization) and expected monthly unit costs + headroom for 2x spike.
3) Camila: schedule a 30-min ops alignment call for Wed where we’ll review SKUs and any network/VPC constraints.

If any of the recap items look off, flag them inline — I’ll update the workbook.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

On Fri, Mar 19, 2027 at 09:45 AM Aaron Mitchell <aaron.mitchell@zenity.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the call — quick answers to the bullets we discussed live.
> 
> - Latency target: yes, 99p <= 150ms is our goal for live chat.
> - TPS: baseline 250 TPS sustained, with marketing-driven spikes up to 600 TPS for ~10–20 minute windows.
> - Token mix: ~70% short chat (<512), ~25% mid (512–1024), ~5% long (>1024).
> - GPU preference: we’ve historically run on A100s but the team is open to H100 if the latency gains justify the premium.
> - VPC: we need a private VPC for any flows touching PHI; non-PHI can go to Hosted.
>
> I’ll populate the token-mix tab in the workbook by EOD Monday.
>
> — Aaron
> Aaron Mitchell | VP Product, Zenity AI
> aaron.mitchell@zenity.ai

From: Aaron Mitchell <aaron.mitchell@zenity.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@zenity.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: hardware preferences, TPS & concurrency follow-up

Camila / Ben —

Quick follow-up after syncing with infra: couple clarifications that will affect the SKU suggestion.

1) Spike shape: the 600 TPS spike is user-driven and lasts 10–25 minutes. During spikes, request length skews shorter (average ~220 tokens) because users trigger quick queries. Sustained 250 TPS has longer average tokens as it includes longer assistant sessions.

2) Concurrency vs sessions: we measure concurrency as active websocket sessions (user browser open). Rough estimate: 600 concurrent sessions corresponded to ~420 active inference calls per second during the last promotion. There’s a ~30% chance of simultaneous long prompts during spikes, which is the real risk to latency.

3) H100 interest: we’ll consider H100 if Redwood can demonstrate single-model 99p latency improvement of at least 20% vs A100 for our workload. If not, preference for A100 with 8-bit quant and a small portion of H100 for tail-heavy low-latency endpoints (e.g., real-time assist).

4) Private VPC: yes for PHI. We need network egress numbers: expected GB/day and whether burstable bandwidth is supported. Also compliance: SOC2 + business associate agreement (BAA) required.

I attached a short note to the workbook (sheet: infra-notes).

Thanks,
Aaron
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mitchell <aaron.mitchell@zenity.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 07:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: hardware preferences, TPS & concurrency follow-up

Aaron / Camila —

Great detail, Aaron — that spike shape and token-length skew are exactly the sort of signals we need. I started a quick sizing pass and attached two artifacts for your review:
- zenity-sizing-workbook.xlsx (updated tab: hw-suggestions) — contains per-SKU throughput estimates using our benchmarking multipliers for short/mid/long token profiles
- redwood-deploy-options.pdf (section 2) — outlines hybrid options (mix H100 for latency-critical endpoints + A100 8-bit for bulk cost savings)

Key notes from the preliminary pass: 
- Performance SKU (H100 pool): 4x H100-80GB nodes (shared pool) modeled to sustain 250 TPS with 2x spike headroom and meet 99p <= 140ms for the short chat profile. Cost estimate: ~$Xk/month (ballpark — to finalize after exact concurrency inputs).
- Cost SKU (A100 + quant): 6x A100-80GB nodes with mixed quantized models should meet baseline 250 TPS and hold spikes to ~450 TPS at degraded 99p (~250–320ms) if we enable aggressive batching; tail latency remains a concern.
- Mixed option: run the public Hosted endpoint for non-PHI, and dedicate a private VPC pool (A100 with optional H100 burst nodes) for PHI flows. This isolates compliance-sensitive traffic while controlling costs.

Questions for Aaron/Karthik to finalize:
1) Can you confirm the expected percentage of traffic that will be flagged PHI at peak? We need that to size the private pool for PHI-only flows.
2) Network egress estimate (GB/day) for model outputs and payloads. If you share a rough number we can validate VPC bandwidth and egress cost assumptions.
3) Do you have a target for acceptable spend band (monthly committed spend) to map to reserved capacity vs on-demand?

I’ll prepare a one-page SKU comparison with headroom scenarios ahead of Wed’s ops call; Camila — happy to present.

Best,
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: hardware preferences, TPS & concurrency follow-up

Thanks Aaron / Ben —

Appreciate the rapid updates. Confirming next steps and ownership so nothing falls through: 
- Aaron / Priya: finalize token-mix + infra-notes in the workbook by EOD Tuesday (we want numbers to run final cost delta).
- Ben: produce the one-page SKU comparison + cost bands (performance vs cost) and include a recommended reserved-commit cadence (monthly vs annual). Please include clear 99p latency estimates for each SKU and the assumptions for quantization.
- Karthik: please include a short note on model variants that are compatible with 8-bit quant (e.g., Llama-2-13B-q8 variants) and any retraining or calibration effort needed to keep quality parity.
- Camila: will put the ops alignment call on Wed 10:00 AM PT — invite sent (30 min). Agenda: review SKUs, VPC constraints, nondisruptive rollout plan (canary + fallback to Hosted).

If you need anything before the call, ping me.

Cheers,
Camila
